question: ‘From fraud to nepotism to revolving doors between the public sector and industry, the stench of impunity is pervasive’, we read in the introduction to a Politico article describing ‘how the EU always gets away with it’1.

The article begins with a presentation of the scandal surrounding Henrik Hololei, who, while he was Director-General of DG MOVE, used free flights in business class on the Qatari national carrier Qatar Airways at a time when the EU was negotiating an Open Skies Agreement with Qatar. An OLAF report reveals how luxury trips, flights, hotels and gifts were also enjoyed by his family.

In response to my question, the Commission stated that ‘OLAF has not found evidence of criminal conduct. It did gather elements indicating a breach of professional obligations.’2 The matter was referred to in the Commission discharge3 and the head of the EPPO criticised the Commission’s transparency. Disciplinary proceedings4 were initiated and Hololei was transferred to a highly paid post.

Meanwhile, according to media reports citing an official with direct knowledge of the proceedings, the Commission finalised its recommendations some time ago and forwarded them to the Secretariat-General for inclusion on the agenda of the College of Commissioners, which is the only body that can issue a decision on the Hololei case5. However, the Commission has so far not put the matter on the agenda. 1.
What is the reason for the delay in concluding the disciplinary proceedings in this shocking case?
Has the Commission gathered additional evidence in the course of the proceedings and shared it with OLAF and the European Public Prosecutor’s Office?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.4.2026) 1. The case was handled in accordance with the applicable rules and procedures, with due respect of the right to be heard of the person concerned. On 29 January 2026, the College of Commissioners concluded the disciplinary procedure with a penalty commensurate to the established facts. 2. The Commission did not gather additional evidence in the course of the disciplinary proceedings.
